{{Short description|Indian automotive manufacturer}} {{Use dmy dates|date=January 2023}} {{Use Indian English|date=January 2023}} {{Infobox company | name = Kinetic Engineering Limited | logo = Kinetic Engineering Limited.svg | caption = | type = | fate = | predecessor = | successor = | founded = {{Start date|1972}} | founder = H. K. Firodia | traded_as = {{BSE|500240}} | hq_location_city = [[Pune]] | hq_location_country = India | hq_location = | area_served = | key_people = [[Arun Firodia]] (chairperson)
[[Ajinkya Firodia]] (Managing Director)
[[Sulajja Firodia Motwani]] (vice-chair) | industry = Automotive | products = [[Kinetic Luna]] | services = | revenue = | operating_income = | net_income = | aum = | assets = | equity = | owner = | num_employees = | parent = Firodia Group | divisions = | subsidiaries = [[Kinetic Honda]] | website = {{URL|kineticindia.com}} | footnotes = | intl = }} '''Kinetic Engineering Limited''' is an Indian automotive manufacturer. The company was founded in the year 1972 by H. K. Firodia. Today it is an automotive component manufacturer which formerly sold two-wheelers under the brand names [[Kinetic Honda]] and later [[Kinetic Motors]]. It introduced the [[Kinetic Luna]] moped which sold well domestically and was exported extensively to [[Argentina]], [[Brazil]], [[Sri Lanka]], and the [[United States]]. Later Kinetic Engineering formed a joint venture with [[Honda Motor Company]] to introduce Kinetic Honda scooters, which had electric start and gearless transmissions. Kinetic and Honda parted ways in 1998 when the [[Firodia]]s bought the majority stake of the joint venture from Honda. In December 2000 Kinetic launches the Challenger 100 motorcycle in India. In October 2001, Kinetic, together with its South Korean partner [[KR Motors|Hyosung]], began production of the GF125 motorcycle, assembled at the Pune plant using components imported from South Korea.{{cite web|url= https://www.afaqs.com/news/3364_kinetic-unveils-gf125-promotion-budget-to-be-rs-5-crore|title= Kinetic unveils GF125; promotion budget to be Rs 5 crore |date=11 October 2001}} This model would also be exported to foreign markets by Hyosung.{{cite web|url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/kinetic-launches-bike-101101101020_1.html|title=Kinetic launches bikes|date=11 October 2001}} In 2002, the Boss 100 motorcycle was launched, equipped with an independently developed four‑stroke single‑cylinder engine. The following year, the Boss models with a 115 cc engine were introduced, along with the Velocity 115 and the sporty Hyosung GF 170 Laser, the latter designed in collaboration with [[KR Motors|Hyosung]] and also intended for export.{{cite web|url=https://rediff.com/business/report/kinetic/20030807.htm|title=Kinetic launches four new bike|date=7 August 2003}} In January 2004, Kinetic acquired from the Italian company [[Italjet]] the production and distribution rights for seven scooters in a deal worth 50 million dollars.{{cite web|url=https://www.telegraphindia.com/business/italjet-goes-for-pillion-ride-with-kinetic/cid/958017|title=Italjet goes for pillion ride with Kinetic|date=13 January 2004}} Specifically, Kinetic intended to manufacture and launch on the Indian market the Italjet Velocifero, Jet Set, Torpedo, Millenium, Jupiter, Dragster and Formula models under the sub‑brand "Italiano", while exporting them under license with the Italjet brand to Europe and North America. The following year, the first model was introduced: the Kinetic Blaze 165, which was essentially the former Italjet Millennium. However, its lukewarm reception in the Indian market (due to the large engine displacement) and the fact that exports to foreign markets never began led to the halt of development and production of the remaining six ex‑Italjet models.{{cite web|url=https://m.economictimes.com/kinetic-rolls-out-blaze-plans-more-italjet-models/articleshow/1632323.cms|title=Kinetic rolls out Blaze, plans more Italjet models|date=9 June 2006}} In January 2006, Kinetic formed an alliance with the Taiwanese manufacturer [[Sanyang Motor|SYM]] to produce scooters in India to be sold under the Kinetic-SYM brand. SYM also acquired about 11.1% of Kinetic's shares.{{cite web|url=https://economictimes.com/kinetic-motor-ties-up-with-taiwans-sym/articleshow/1366732.cms |title=Kinetic Motor ties up with Taiwan's SYM|date=11 January 2006}} This partnership made it possible to launch the Flyte 125 scooter in 2007, derived from the SYM Xpro 125.{{cite web|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/kinetic-sym-on-a-flyte/articleshow/2632490.cms|title=Kinetic-SYM on a 'Flyte'|date=19 December 2007}} In 2008, Kinetic entered into a joint venture with [[Mahindra & Mahindra|Mahindra Automobiles]], where Mahindra held an 80% stake.''[[International Business Times]]'', 31 July 2008, "Mahindra & Mahindra buys Kinetic Motor for Rs.110 crore, forays into two-wheeler market" by Surojit Chatterjee. By this joint venture, Mahindra acquired the two-wheeler manufacturing facilities as well as the then selling brands of Kinetic. After ceasing two-wheeler manufacturing, Kinetic Engineering produces and exports automotive components. Kinetic Motors resumed operations in January 2011 and has announced plans to produce [[electric vehicle]]s under the newly launched Kinetic Green Brand. In February 2014, Kinetic sold its stake in Mahindra Two-Wheelers to Samena Capital for 182 [[crore]] [[rupee]]s.{{cite web|title=Kinetic Engineering sells its Stake in Mahindra for 182 Crores|url=http://news.biharprabha.com/2014/02/kinetic-engineering-sells-its-stake-in-mahindra-for-182-crores/|work=IANS|publisher=news.biharprabha.com|access-date=25 February 2014}} In January 2022, Kinetic entered into a partnership with the Chinese group Aima Technology for the development and production in India of electric scooters using Aima's technologies.{{cite web|url=https://www.financialexpress.com/auto/bike-news/kinetic-green-to-enter-ev-two-wheeler-market-with-chinas-aima/2416083/|title=Kinetic Green to enter EV two-wheeler market with China’s Aima|date=22 January 2022}} A new version of the Luna called the [[Kinetic E-Luna|E-Luna]] launched in February 2024.{{Cite web |author=MotorLane's Desk |date=2024-02-07 |title=New Kinetic Luna Electric launched Starting At Rs. 69,990/- MotorLane - Worlds No.1 Automotive Website |url=https://motorlane.in/ev-scooters/kinetic-luna-electric-launched-at-69990/ |access-date=2024-02-08 |language=en-US}} The prebookings were open from on 26 Jan 2024 .{{Cite web |url=https://www.bikedekho.com/kinetic/luna-electric?amp=1 |access-date=2024-01-27 |website=www.bikedekho.com |title=Kinetic Green e Luna Price- Range, Charging Time, Speed, Images & Specs }}{{Cite news |title=Kinetic E-Luna features revealed: Check its price and specifications |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/renewables/kinetic-e-luna-features-revealed-check-its-price-and-specifications/articleshow/107141490.cms |access-date=2024-01-27 |website=[[The Economic Times]]|date=25 January 2024 }} At present the company produce electric two and three wheelers.{{Cite web |title=Kinetic Engineering to take EV route to re-enter two-wheeler market - The Economic Times |url=https://m.economictimes.com/industry/auto/two-wheelers-three-wheelers/kinetic-engineering-to-take-ev-route-to-re-enter-two-wheeler-market/articleshow/117436290.cms |access-date=2025-01-23 |website=m.economictimes.com}} In July 2025, the joint venture "Kinetic Green Tonino Lamborghini Pvt Ltd." is established in Pune for the production of luxury golf carts designed by [[Tonino Lamborghini]].{{cite web|url= https://businessindia.co/amp/story/magazine/mobility/kinetic-green-enters-a-new-lane|title= Kinetic Green enters a new lane|date=29 July 2025}} Also in the same month the Kinetic DX electric scooter is launched.{{cite web|url= https://www.bikewale.com/news/new-kinetic-dx-electric-scooter-launched-in-india-at-rs-111-lakh/|title= New Kinetic DX Electric Scooter Launched in India at Rs. 1.11 Lakh |date=28 July 2025}} Designed by Alessandro Tartarini and manufactured at the Ahilya Nagar plant, its styling is inspired by the Kinetic Honda DX produced in India in the 1980s (itself derived from the [[Honda NH series|Honda NH Lead]]).{{cite web|url= https://kineticindia.com/tag/kinetic-dx-design/|title=Kinetic DX EV: the iconic scooter returns in an electric avatar|date=29 August 2025}} ==Kinetic Luna== [[File:Kinetic Luna Super.JPG|thumb|Kinetic Luna Super in Sri Lanka 2013]] '''Kinetic Luna''' is a 50 cc [[moped]] that was introduced by [[Kinetic Engineering]] in India in 1972 and based on the italian [[Piaggio Ciao]].{{cite web|title=Kinetic Luna|url=http://www.iloveindia.com/bikes/kinetic-engineering/luna.html|accessdate=13 Aug 2012}} The Kinetic Luna continues to be produced and marketed in India. It is marketed in the US as '''Kinetic TFR'''. A 35 cc version, the Luna Wings, was also produced. The original Luna of 1972 was a licensed copy of [[Piaggio Ciao]] moped. It has since been updated by Kinetic until the end of production in early 2000s. ===Models=== Luna kinetic *Luna TFR (out of production) *Luna TFR Plus *Luna Double plus *Luna Wings *Luna Magnum *Luna Super ==Kinetic E-Luna== {{Infobox motorcycle | name = Kinetic E-Luna | image = | caption = | manufacturer =Kinetic Engineering Limited | production =2024–present | predecessor =[[Kinetic Luna]] | successor = | class =Electric Moped | top_speed =60 kph | power =3kWh | torque = | suspension =Telescopic Fork front suspension and dual shock rear suspension | brakes = | tires = | wheelbase = | length =1985mm | width =735mm | height =1036mm | seat_height =760mm | dry_weight =96kg | range =~100km | related = }} The '''Kinetic E-Luna''' is an [[Electric motorcycles and scooters|Electric bike]] build by Kinetic Green and based on the Kinetic Luna. It was launched on February 7, 2024.{{Cite web |date=2024-01-29 |title=E-Luna Price Announcement To Take Place On February 7th |url=https://www.timesnownews.com/auto/electric-vehicles/e-luna-price-announcement-to-take-place-on-february-7th-article-107223034 |access-date=2024-01-29 |website=TimesNow |language=en}}{{Cite web |last=Vijay |first=Amit |date=29 January 2024 |title=Autocar India |url=https://www.autocarindia.com/bike-news/piyush-pandey-to-recreate-chal-meri-luna-magic-for-kinetic-e-luna-430444 |access-date=29 January 2024 |website=AutoCar India}}{{Cite news |title=Kinetic E-Luna features revealed: Check its price and specifications |work=The Economic Times |date=25 January 2024 |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/renewables/kinetic-e-luna-features-revealed-check-its-price-and-specifications/articleshow/107141490.cms |access-date=2024-01-29 }} Kinetic announced that it would start bookings for the E-Luna on 26 January with a reservation fee of ₹500.{{Cite news |date=2024-01-25 |title=Iconic Kinetic Luna to return as e-moped in Feb: Bookings begin on Republic Day |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/auto/electric-bikes/iconic-kinetic-luna-emoped-bookings-start-on-republic-day/articleshow/107137875.cms |access-date=2024-01-29 |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257}} ===Development=== Kinetic had started a pilot project around September 2023 in some locations of [[Maharashtra]] with an aim to sell the vehicle to a couple of thousand people and gather customer feedback using [[prototype]] models, which were met with success.{{Cite web |last=Singh |first=Anjali |date=29 January 2024 |title=Kinetic Green to launch E-Luna in February, bookings start on January 26 |url=https://www.business-standard.com/amp/companies/news/kinetic-green-to-launch-e-luna-in-february-bookings-start-on-january-26-124012500726_1.html |access-date=29 January 2024 |website=Business Standard}} The company intends to target the {{INR}}25,000-30,000 monthly income group which uses public transportation, such as shared automobiles or local buses. The company is aiming for 5,000 electric Lunas per month.{{clarify|hires? Production?do tell|date=February 2024}} The company hopes to gross close to {{INR }}30 crore annually{{Cite web |author=HT Auto Desk|date=2024-01-25 |title=Remember Kinetic Luna? Now get ready for E-Luna with bookings at ₹500 |url=https://auto.hindustantimes.com/auto/electric-vehicles/remember-kinetic-luna-now-get-ready-for-e-luna-with-bookings-at-rs-500-41706154965497.html |access-date=2024-01-29 |website=HT Auto |language=en}} ===Design=== The e-Luna was introduced with three battery packs. The first batch will have a 2 kWh battery pack which will give a range of 80 km. The company also hopes to introduce a 1.5 kWh battery pack for Tier 2 and Tier 3 markets for a 40–45 km range, and a 3 kWh battery pack, which will give a range of 100–125 km, . the Kinetic E-Luna comes with [[Telescopic fork|Telescopic Fork front suspensions]] and dual shock rear suspension. It would have a top speed of around 60 kph, a weight of {{cvt|96|kg|lb}}, a seat height of {{cvt|760|mm}}, and a ground clearance of 170 mm. The batteries will be made inhouse with three different variants – chargeable, removable and swappable.{{Cite news |last=Anand |first=N. |date=2024-01-27 |title=Kinetic Green plans a big role in e2w segment with Luna |url=https://www.thehindu.com/business/kinetic-green-plans-a-big-role-in-e2w-segment-with-luna/article67782747.ece |access-date=2024-01-29 |work=The Hindu |language=en-IN |issn=0971-751X}} The model will come with four drive modes - ECO, City, Speed and Sport. It will be more rugged, with an improved halogen headlight and white color-turned indicators on the side. It will have a fully digital console and an app for connectivity control.{{Cite web |author=HT Auto Desk|date=2024-02-06 |title=Kinetic Green E-Luna electric moped to be launched tomorrow: What to expect? |url=https://auto.hindustantimes.com/auto/electric-vehicles/kinetic-green-e-luna-electric-moped-to-be-launched-tomorrow-what-to-expect-41707212841327.html |access-date=2024-02-07 |website=HT Auto |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2024-02-07 |title=Kinetic Green to revive Luna in electric avatar today |url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/kinetic-green-to-revive-luna-in-electric-avatar-today-12212751.html |access-date=2024-02-07 |website=Moneycontrol}} In December 2024, Kinetic unveiled plans to extend the range of the moped using a 4.3kWh battery pack with a range of 250 kilometres. It was planned to be available by January 2025.{{Cite news |title=Kinetic Green confirms E-Luna variant with range of two electric scooters: Details |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/auto/electric-bikes/kinetic-green-confirms-e-luna-variant-with-range-of-two-electric-scooters-details/articleshow/115903033.cms |access-date=2024-12-04 |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257}} == See also == * [[H. Kinetic Engineering Limited is an Indian automotive manufacturer. The company was founded in the year 1972 by H. K. Firodia. Today it is an automotive component manufacturer which formerly sold two-wheelers under the brand names Kinetic Honda and later Kinetic Motors. It introduced the Kinetic Luna moped which sold well domestically and was exported extensively to Argentina, Brazil, Sri Lanka, and the United States.
Later Kinetic Engineering formed a joint venture with Honda Motor Company to introduce Kinetic Honda scooters, which had electric start and gearless transmissions. Kinetic and Honda parted ways in 1998 when the Firodias bought the majority stake of the joint venture from Honda. 
In December 2000 Kinetic launches the Challenger 100 motorcycle in India.
In October 2001, Kinetic, together with its South Korean partner Hyosung, began production of the GF125 motorcycle, assembled at the Pune plant using components imported from South Korea. This model would also be exported to foreign markets by Hyosung.
In 2002, the Boss 100 motorcycle was launched, equipped with an independently developed four‑stroke single‑cylinder engine. The following year, the Boss models with a 115 cc engine were introduced, along with the Velocity 115 and the sporty Hyosung GF 170 Laser, the latter designed in collaboration with Hyosung and also intended for export.
In January 2004, Kinetic acquired from the Italian company Italjet the production and distribution rights for seven scooters in a deal worth 50 million dollars.
Specifically, Kinetic intended to manufacture and launch on the Indian market the Italjet Velocifero, Jet Set, Torpedo, Millenium, Jupiter, Dragster and Formula models under the sub‑brand "Italiano", while exporting them under license with the Italjet brand to Europe and North America. The following year, the first model was introduced: the Kinetic Blaze 165, which was essentially the former Italjet Millennium. However, its lukewarm reception in the Indian market (due to the large engine displacement) and the fact that exports to foreign markets never began led to the halt of development and production of the remaining six ex‑Italjet models.
In January 2006, Kinetic formed an alliance with the Taiwanese manufacturer SYM to produce scooters in India to be sold under the Kinetic-SYM brand. SYM also acquired about 11.1% of Kinetic's shares. This partnership made it possible to launch the Flyte 125 scooter in 2007, derived from the SYM Xpro 125.
In 2008, Kinetic entered into a joint venture with Mahindra Automobiles, where Mahindra held an 80% stake. By this joint venture, Mahindra acquired the two-wheeler manufacturing facilities as well as the then selling brands of Kinetic.
After ceasing two-wheeler manufacturing, Kinetic Engineering produces and exports automotive components. Kinetic Motors resumed operations in January 2011 and has announced plans to produce electric vehicles under the newly launched Kinetic Green Brand. 
In February 2014, Kinetic sold its stake in Mahindra Two-Wheelers to Samena Capital for 182 crore rupees.
In January 2022, Kinetic entered into a partnership with the Chinese group Aima Technology for the development and production in India of electric scooters using Aima's technologies.
A new version of the Luna called the E-Luna launched in February 2024. The prebookings were open from on 26 Jan 2024 .
At present the company produce electric two and three wheelers.
In July 2025, the joint venture "Kinetic Green Tonino Lamborghini Pvt Ltd." is established in Pune for the production of luxury golf carts designed by Tonino Lamborghini. 
Also in the same month the Kinetic DX electric scooter is launched. Designed by Alessandro Tartarini and manufactured at the Ahilya Nagar plant, its styling is inspired by the Kinetic Honda DX produced in India in the 1980s (itself derived from the Honda NH Lead).
